decision.summary: The Federal Reserve kept its target for the federal funds rate unchanged at 1-1/4 percent.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to keep its target for the federal funds rate unchanged at 1-1/4 percent.
changes.explanation: The Fed left interest rates steady because it views current monetary policy as supportive of economic activity.

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee continues to believe that this accommodative stance of monetary policy, coupled with still robust underlying growth in productivity, is providing important ongoing support to economic activity.

In these circumstances, the Committee believes that, against the background of its long-run goals of price stability and sustainable economic growth and of the information currently available, the risks are balanced with respect to the prospects for both goals for the foreseeable future.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 13.36% APR costs about $55.67 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.06% and moved 0 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.13% would not change.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 5.9%, and employers added an average of 12k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.3% over the past year (November 2002); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.7%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 1.6% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +2 bp on the day.

card.whats_next: The statement signals that the Committee views the risks to its goals as balanced for the foreseeable future. Future meetings will depend on incoming economic indicators to see how the economy works through its soft spot.
